answer: An agent economy can require every account to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it can submit jobs, and let randomly selected peers challenge suspicious identities. If several accounts share control or collude, a fraud proof can trigger a penalty and remove their access; honest agents earn fees by checking challenges. A canyon of independent reviewers, a knoll of new accounts, or a mesa of established agents does not change the rule: each Sybil identity needs its own capital at risk, so scaling the attack ties up funds and exposes them to loss.
